claim: A 2023 benchmark built on Only Connect walls (Remote Associates Test style with deliberate red herrings) was made to test whether LLMs show the Einstellung/fixation effect.
quote: Large Language Models are Fixated by Red Herrings
title: Large Language Models are Fixated by Red Herrings: Exploring Creative Problem Solving and Einstellung Effect using the Only Connect Wall Dataset
transfer: Red-herring items are a test set for fixation. Run it before and after any doubt or reframing step to see if the step lowers fixation. Result numbers not read.

claim: Stronger reasoning models fall into Einstellung traps less often than weaker ones, and reached human-level scores on an adversarial medical benchmark (mARC) built to trigger Einstellung.
quote: achieving human-level performance on mARC
authors: Shidara, Prem, Kim, Podlasek, Liu, Alaa, Bernardo
title: Advances in LLM Reasoning Enable Flexibility in Clinical Problem-Solving
transfer: Reasoning effort itself reduces rigid pattern use. Spend thinking tokens on problems that look like a familiar pattern but carry a twist; do not add forced doubt everywhere.

claim: On mARC the top 5 models answered 55% to 70% correctly, with high confidence, on questions physicians commonly miss.
quote: the top 5 performing models answered 55% to 70% correctly with high confidence
title: Advances in LLM Reasoning Enable Flexibility in Clinical Problem-Solving
transfer: High stated confidence is not a sign of avoiding the trap; do not use model confidence alone as the trigger for doubt.

claim: LLM idea generation shows fixation: models repeatedly converge on familiar solution spaces; simple prompting strategies can raise originality but outputs stay homogeneous across models.
quote: simple prompting strategies can boost the originality of solutions
title: IDEAFix: Evaluation Framework for Creative Defixation Prompting in LLMs
transfer: Defixation cues (surprising or negatively framed keywords) are cheap divergence steps for the open-ended branch only. The keyword detail came from a search summary, not the abstract.

claim: In LLMs, early outputs constrain later ones (fixation). Chain-of-thought prompting reduced fixation in LLMs but not in humans.
quote: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting reduces fixation by encouraging structured reasoning (only in LLMs, not humans)
title: Examining and Addressing Barriers to Diversity in LLM-Generated Ideas
transfer: Ask for reasoning before each new idea in a divergence pass. Generate ideas in separate calls, not one long list, so earlier ideas do not anchor later ones.

claim: Ordinary personas used as sampling cues improved knowledge partitioning (diversity) better than famous creative-entrepreneur personas; combining CoT with personas gave idea diversity above humans.
quote: Combining both approaches produces the highest idea diversity, outperforming humans.
title: Examining and Addressing Barriers to Diversity in LLM-Generated Ideas
transfer: For divergence cards, vary the role across calls using ordinary, varied people, not 'genius'. Fits Weisberg's ordinary-thinking view.

claim: Asking an LLM to act as a 'genius' or a demographic persona did not reliably raise creativity on the Divergent Association Task; raising temperature helped novelty only up to a point, then output became nonsensical.
quote: top-tier human performers consistently outscoring even the most advanced models
title: Divergent Association Task, 9,198 humans vs about 215,000 LLM observations
transfer: Do not rely on 'be a genius' prompts or high temperature for divergence. Quote is from a secondary summary (Chinese Academy of Sciences page); paper not opened. Another secondary article gave a different journal and sample, so details are uncertain.

claim: LLMs can beat the average human on the Divergent Association Task and approach human creative writing, but the best models are still largely surpassed by highly creative people.
quote: even the top performing LLMs are still largely surpassed by highly creative individuals
authors: Bellemare-Pepin, Lespinasse, Tholke, Harel, Mathewson, Olson, Bengio, Jerbi and others
title: Divergent Creativity in Humans and Large Language Models
transfer: Average-level divergence is easy for a model; the gap is at the top tail. Use many samples plus a strong selector to reach the tail.

claim: Meta-analysis of 28 studies: GenAI and humans do not differ in creative performance (g=-0.05); humans helped by GenAI beat unaided humans (g=0.27); GenAI reduces the diversity of ideas in human-AI work (g=-0.86).
quote: GenAI has a significant negative effect on the diversity of ideas
title: Generative AI and Creativity: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta-Analysis
transfer: Quality of single ideas is not the weak point; diversity is. Put the diversity step in the program, and measure distinct ideas, not average quality.

claim: A second 2025 meta-analysis (17 studies, 115 effect sizes) found a small non-significant pooled effect favouring GenAI, driven by a few large effects, and no support that GenAI has surpassed humans at idea generation.
quote: no empirical support suggests that GenAI has surpassed humans in creative idea generation
title: GenAI vs human creativity meta-analysis
transfer: Treat claims of AI creativity superiority as unsettled; judge our own wins by distinct-answer counts plus an objective judge. Quote is from a search summary.

claim: Open-ended LLM answers are homogeneous within a model and across models (Artificial Hivemind), shown on 26K real open-ended queries with 31,250 human annotations.
quote: pronounced Artificial Hivemind effect in open-ended generation of LMs
title: Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (and Beyond)
transfer: Using other models for variety will not help much; variety must come from the procedure (forced different frames), as our NoveltyBench result shows. LM judges are also less calibrated on contested responses.

claim: Between-participants experiment: support from an AI image generator raised fixation on an initial example; AI users made fewer, less varied, less original ideas than baseline.
quote: Participants who used AI produced fewer ideas, with less variety and lower originality compared to a baseline.
title: The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking
transfer: This is humans fixating on AI output. For our agent: an example shown to the model also anchors it, so show no example, or opposing ones, in divergence calls.

claim: In a hackathon-style engineering design study, ChatGPT fixated on the last item in a supplied list and recommended it for every prototype.
quote: often fixated on specific prompt details, such as the final machine on a list of manufacturing capabilities
title: ChatGPT as an inventor: Eliciting the strengths and weaknesses of current large language models against humans in engineering design
transfer: Shuffle the order of options and lists across calls to cancel position anchoring. Quote is from a search summary, not the paper.

claim: Ideation stage: LLM-generated research ideas were judged more novel than expert ideas (p<0.05) and slightly weaker on feasibility, in a study with over 100 NLP researchers.
quote: LLM-generated ideas are judged as more novel (p < 0.05)
title: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
transfer: Novelty is cheap for a model; selection and feasibility are the work. A listing page also names failed LLM self-evaluation and lack of diversity as open problems.

claim: After 43 experts spent over 100 hours executing ideas, LLM ideas lost significantly more score than human ideas on novelty, excitement, effectiveness and overall, and rankings flipped on many metrics.
quote: the scores of the LLM-generated ideas decrease significantly more
title: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
transfer: Never rank ideas by how they look on paper. Run them (training run, tests) as the judge, as in our architecture search. Supports objective pruning.

claim: Original Einstellung result in chess: a familiar solution blocked experts from finding a better one, cutting their performance to that of players about three standard deviations weaker; but more expert players were less prone to the effect.
quote: inflexibility of experts is both reality and myth
title: Inflexibility of experts: Reality or myth? Quantifying the Einstellung effect in chess masters
transfer: Older than 2018 but the base of the field. Fixation is a behaviour (first idea steers attention), so it is testable in an agent. Details from a search summary; PDF not opened.

claim: Eye tracking shows the Einstellung effect works by biasing attention to features tied to the familiar solution; when the familiar move was a blunder, all experts and most novices avoided it.
quote: biasing attention towards problem features that are associated with the familiar solution rather than the optimal solution
title: The Mechanisms and Boundary Conditions of the Einstellung Effect in Chess: Evidence from Eye Movements
transfer: Doubt is needed when the familiar answer is merely suboptimal, not clearly wrong. Check the first answer with a cheap test, and re-read the problem for features the first idea ignored. Pre-2018 work.

claim: Deliberate practice meta-analysis: 88 studies, 11,135 participants; deliberate practice explained about 12 percent of performance differences overall, 26% in games, 21% music, 18% sports, 4% education, under 1% professions.
quote: Deliberate practice accounted for only about 12 percent of individual differences
title: Deliberate practice and performance in music, games, sports, education, and professions: A meta-analysis
transfer: TRAIT/HISTORY: practice hours cannot transfer to a model at inference time. Only the structure (focused feedback on weak spots) maps to training, which we do not do. Pre-2018; from search summaries, page not opened.

claim: A 2020 review asks whether the deliberate practice view is defensible as a testable theory; Ericsson replied that the definition had not changed, so the dispute over what counts as deliberate practice is open.
quote: Is the Deliberate Practice View Defensible? A Review of Evidence and Discussion of Issues
title: Is the Deliberate Practice View Defensible? A Review of Evidence and Discussion of Issues
transfer: none. Mark as TRAIT/HISTORY: cannot transfer. The page was blocked by a browser check, so only the title and the existence of Ericsson's reply were confirmed by search.

claim: Weisberg's ordinary-thinking view: creative thinking is the same as ordinary thinking, with no special outside-the-box process; it predicts analytic processes in all cases of creativity and that ordinary people can be creative; tested on Watson and Crick's DNA model and Picasso's Guernica.
quote: There is no special kind of thinking – no outside the box thinking – which serves in the creation of new ideas.
title: Creativity: Understanding Innovation in Problem Solving, Science, Invention, and the Arts
venue: Wiley (book); later Rethinking Creativity, Cambridge UP
transfer: Build divergence from ordinary steps (recall, analogy, small changes) plus a selector, not a special creative mode. Fits our result that forced variety plus pruning works. Quote came from a chapter summary found by search.

claim: Chunking theory (Chase and Simon) says chess skill comes from storing thousands of chunks in long-term memory; template theory (Gobet and Simon) adds slotted structures; recall of random positions and very brief presentations best tell the theories apart.
quote: recall of random and distorted positions, very brief presentations, and interference studies
title: Expert memory: A comparison of four theories
transfer: Chunks map to a stored library of solved patterns and lessons that the agent retrieves (our lessons ledger). Pre-2018. Quote is a fragment of a search summary, so treat as not verbatim.

claim: No study found that applies Getzels and Csikszentmihalyi problem finding to LLM agents directly; closest is CoQuest, where a 20-person study found higher AI initiative gave more creative research questions at the cost of user experience.
quote: a higher degree of AI initiative led to co-creation outcomes with enhanced creativity
title: CoQuest: Exploring Research Question Co-Creation with an LLM-based Agent
transfer: A gap in the literature. A problem-finding step (write several framings of the task and pick one before solving) has no direct LLM evidence; test it ourselves, only on open tasks.
